provisions.textEn:
1. In derogation of Article 27e(1), the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered the suspect's detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the parents or guardian of the deprivation of liberty and the reasons for it as soon as possible. The parents or guardian shall furthermore receive a notification of the rights provided for in Article 488aa.
  2. The notification of rights provided for in the first paragraph, shall not take place when: (a) this would contrary to the interests of the suspect; (b) the notification is not possible because despite reasonable efforts the parents or guardian cannot be reached or identified.
  3. In the case referred to in paragraph 2, the information shall be provided to a confidant. If no confidant has been nominated, the information shall be provided to the Child Care and Protection Board.
  4. Where the circumstances, referred to in paragraph 2, cease to exist, the information shall be provided to the parents or guardian.

items.comment:
This provision has been transposed in part through amendments to the Surrender of Persons Act (Overleveringswet), i.e. the Act implementing Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA on the European arrest warrant and the surrender procedures between Member States. For the other part, the Surrender of Persons Act was considered to be already compliant with the Directive. The relevant provisions have been set out below, but - to facilitate understanding of his this broad provision has been transposed precisely - the following starts with providing an overview of which provisions precisely transpose which rights.


  • The application of Article 4 of the Directive (right to information) in European arrest warrant (EAW) proceedings has been effectuated through amending Article 17(3) of the Surrender of Persons Act in which Articles 27e of the Dutch Code of Criminal Procedure (CCP) and 488ab CCP have been declared to apply mutatis mutandis.
  • The application of Article 5 of the Directive (right to have the holder of parental responsibility informed) in EAW proceedings has been effectuated through amending Article 17(3) of the Surrender of Persons Act in which Article 488b CCP has been declared to apply mutatis mutandis.
  • The application of Article 6 of the Directive (right to assistance by a lawyer) in EAW proceedings has already been effectuated in the course of transposing Directive 2013/48/EU. Pursuant to Article 43a of the Surrender of Persons Act, the right of access to a lawyer already applies in EAW prceedings, also for children. No additional transposition measures were considered necessary.
  • The application of Article 8 of the Directive (right to a medical examination) in EAW proceedings has not been effectuated. It seems to us that a mistake has been made, perhaps accidentally. According to the explanatory memorandum to the implementation proposal, the application of Article 8 in EAW proceedings had to be effectuated through amending Article 21(1) of the Surrender of Persons Act , namely by means of declaring Article 489a CCP to apply mutatis mutandis. Article 21(1) of the Surrender of Persons Act does not, however, contain a reference to Article 489a CCP. It does refer to Article 17(3), which mutatis mutandis application does result in the right to be informed on a number of rights, but even here the right to a medical examination has not been included, neither for adults, nor for children. Therefore, our conclusion is this part of Article 17 of the Directive has not been transposed.
  • With respect to the application of Article 10 of the Directive (limitation of deprivation of liberty) in EAW proceedings, it was stated that Articles 61 and 22 of the Surender of Persons Act already comply with the requirements of the Directive. Article 61 of the Surrender Persons Act stipulates that persons who have been deprived of liberty under the Surrender of Persons Act are treated equally as suspects who has been deprived of liberty under the CCP. Moreover, the strict terms for deciding on EAW's envisaged in Article 22 of the Surrender of Persons Act must further guarantee that deprivation of liberty is significantly limited in time. Consequently, the requirements of Article 10 of the Directive must be considered to be met in EAW proceedings too. See further the comments made with respect to the transposition of Article 10 of the Directive.
  • With respect to the application of Article 11 of the Directive (alternatives to detention) in EAW proceedings, it was stated that Article 61 of the Surrender of Persons Act, already complies with the requirements of the Directive. Article 61 of the Surrender Persons Act stipulates that persons who have been deprived of liberty under the Surrender of Persons Act are treated equally as suspects who has been deprived of liberty under the CCP. Consequently, the alternatives to detention, envisaged in the CCP apply mutatis mutandis in EAW proceedings. See also the comments made with respect to the transposition of Article 11 of the Directive.
  • With respect to the application of Article 12 of the Directive (right to specific treatmemt n the case of deprivation of liberty) in EAW proceedings, it was stated that Article 61 of the Surrender of Persons Act, already complies with the requirements of the Directive. Article 61 of the Surrender Persons Act stipulates that persons who have been deprived of liberty under the Surrender of Persons Act are treated equally as suspects who has been deprived of liberty under the CCP. Consequently, children in detention receive a specific treatment. See further the comments made with respect to the transposition of Article 12 of the Directive.
  • The application of Article 13 of the Directive (timely and diligent treatment of cases) in EAW proceedings was - like in ordinary criminal proceedings - not considered requiring transposing legislation. See the comments made with respect to the transposition of this provision.
  • The application of Article 14 of the Directive (right to protection of privacy) in EAW proceedings was considered to be ensured already, first because Article 25 of the Surrender of Persons Act does provide for the possibility to have court hearings held behind closed doors, and, secondly through the other - already existing - regulations regarding the protection of privacy. For the latter, see the comments made with respect to the transposition of Article 14 of the Directive.
  • The application of Article 15 of the Directive (right to be accompanied during proceedings) in EAW proceedings has been effectuated through, first, the adoption of Article 62 of the Surrender of Persons act (in which Article 490(1) and (3) CCP has been declared to apply mutatis mutandis, and, secondly, through amendments of Articles 21, 24 and 25 of the Surrender of Persons Act. These amendments entail the adoption of new paragraphs in which the right of the child to be accompanied was laid down for the various stages of the surrender proceedins.
  • With respect to the application of Article 18 of the Directive (right to legal aid) in EAW proceedings, the same applies as with regard to the application of Article 6 in EAW proceedings. See above.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that national law in relation to legal aid guarantees the effective exercise of the right to be assisted by a lawyer pursuant to Article 6.
items.heading: Article 18

provisions.comment: Own translation; no official translation available.
provisions.textEn:
1. If a suspect has been arrested, the public prosecutor or the assistant public prosecutor to have ordered his detention for investigation at the arraignment shall notify the governing body of the Legal Aid Board immediately, in order that the governing body assign a lawyer. This notification need not take place if the suspect or accused person has chosen a lawyer and this lawyer or their replacement is available promptly.
  2. Article 28a does not apply.
  3. If a suspect has been sent away in the evening hours because no lawyer is available, and simultaneously has been informed that he will be questioned the next day, paragraph 1 applies to that interview.

provisions.comment: Own translation: no official translation available
provisions.textEn:
1. Without prejudice to Article 489(1), a defence counsel shall be assigned to the suspect without counsel by the governing body of the Legal Aid Board, after it has been informed that prosecution other than by punishment order has been instituted against the suspect in relation to an offence for which the district court, not being a sub-district court, is competent in first instance. Article 40(2) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  2. The public prosecutor shall summon the suspect to be questioned if the punishment order he intends to impose involves either community service, as referred to in Article 77f(2) of the Criminal Code, of more than 22 hours, or fines or financial compensations that separately or together amount to more than 200 euros. A defence counsel shall be assigned to the suspect without counsel by the governing body of the Legal Aid Board, after it has been informed about this intention by the Public Prosecution Service. When the suspect is summoned, he shall be informed of his right to be assisted by a lawyer.
  3. A defence counsel shall be assigned ex officio by the governing body of the Legal Aid Board if the convicted offender, in view of the the nature of the questioning to be conducted pursuant to Articles 77u or 77ee(1) in conjunction with Article 14i(3) of the Dutch Criminal Code, requires his assistance.
  4. The assignment pursuant to paragraph 3 shall be arranged by order of the presiding judge of the District Court, or, when appeal has been filed against the final judgment rendered at the court of first instance, by the presiding judge of the Court of Appeal.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings and children who are requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 19

provisions.comment: Translation partly borrowed from: http://www.ejtn.eu/PageFiles/6533/2014%20seminars/Omsenie/WetboekvanStrafvordering_ENG_PV.pdf. Unofficial translation; official translation not available.
provisions.textEn:
1. Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning serious offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the suspect who was not acquitted of the entire indictment.

2. Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning minor offences, rendered by the District Court as final judgment or in the course of the hearing, by the public prosecutor with the court which rendered the judgment, and by the suspect who was not acquitted of the entire indictment, unless in this regard in the final judgment:

a. under application of Article 9a of the Criminal Code, a punishment or measure was not imposed, or

b. no other punishment or measure was imposed than a fine up to a maximum – or, where two or more fines were imposed in the judgment, fines up to a joint maximum – of € 50.

3.In derogation of paragraph 2, the suspect may file an appeal against a judgment rendered in absentia as referred to in paragraph (2)(a) and (b), if the summons or notice to appear at the court session of the court of first instance or the notice to appear at the court session at a later date was not given to or served on the defendant in person and no other circumstance has occurred from which it follows that the date of the court session or of the court session at a later date was known to the defendant beforehand. The preceding sentence shall not apply in the event that the summons or appearance notice was lawfully served on the defendant in accordance with Article 588a within six weeks after the defendant filed an objection to the judgment in absentia under the terms of Article 257e.  

4.The judgments, referred to in paragraphs (2)(a) and (b), which are not open to appeal, shall not be open to appeal in cassation either, unless in the case of a violation of a bye-law of a province, a municipality, a water control authority, or a public body established under application of the Joint Regulations Act [Wet Gemeenschappelijke Regelingen].

5. If at the court of first instance criminal offences have been tried jointly by the District Court, then the suspect may only file an appeal in regard of those joint cases in which he was not acquitted of the entire indictment.

provisions.comment: Translation partly borrowed from: http://www.ejtn.eu/PageFiles/6533/2014%20seminars/Omsenie/WetboekvanStrafvordering_ENG_PV.pdf. Unofficial translation; official translation not available.
provisions.textEn:
1. Appeal in cassation may be filed against judgments concerning serious offences pronounced by the Courts of Appeal by the Public Prosecution Service attached to the court which rendered the judgment, and by the suspect.

2. Appeal may be filed against judgments concerning minor offences, pronounced by the Courts of Appeal by the Public Prosecution Service attached to the court which rendered the judgment, and by the suspect, unless in this regard in the final judgment:

a. under application of Article 9a of the Criminal Code, a punishment or measure was not imposed, or

b. no other punishment or measure was imposed than a fine up to a maximum – or, where two or more fines were imposed in the judgment, fines up to a joint maximum – of EUR 250.

3. Appeal in cassation may nevertheless be filed against the judgments, referred to in paragraph (2)(a) and (b), in the case of a violation of a bye-law of a province, a municipality, a water control authority, or a public body established under application of the Joint Regulations Act.

4. Appeal shall suspend the legal effects of appeal in cassation; if a judgment is rendered on one or more of the questions, referred to in Articles 351 and 352, by the lower court, the appeal in cassation filed shall be cancelled.

items.comment: The official position of the Ministry of Justice and Security is that the right to remedies has sufficiently been covered by existing provisions on appeal and cassation.

items.heading: Article 20

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
The Dutch Ministry of Justice and Security has taken the position that explicit transposition of Article 20 is not required. It has pointed out that current educational and training programmes for judges and public prosecutors do provide possibilities to specialise in the field of juvenile criminal law. The same applies for the police. With respect to the independent profession of defence laywers, the responsibility to provide for specific education and training in this area falls under its own autonomous responsibility. It is currently the case that the profession does stipulate minimum requirements for lawyers to represent children in criminal cases.

With respect to staff of detention facilities and other relevant professions, the required specialisation is being safeguarded through a national registration system (Quality Register Youth Care, Kwaliteitsregister Jeugdzorg), for which educational requirements apply.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that staff of law enforcement authorities and of detention facilities who handle cases involving children, receive specific training to a level appropriate to their contact with children with regard to children's rights, appropriate questioning techniques, child psychology, and communication in a language adapted to the child.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See comments above.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Member States, and with due respect for the role of those responsible for the training of judges and prosecutors, Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that judges and prosecutors who deal with criminal proceedings involving children have specific competence in that field, effective access to specific training, or both.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See comments above.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of specific training as referred to in paragraph 2 to lawyers who deal with criminal proceedings involving children.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See comments above.

items.text: 4. Through their public services or by funding child support organisations, Member States shall encourage initiatives enabling those providing children with support and restorative justice services to receive adequate training to a level appropriate to their contact with children and observe professional standards to ensure such services are provided in an impartial, respectful and professional manner.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: See comments above.
